sourcedFrom: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 (2016 revision; cached from a 2025 capture of Savage's own document host)
cleanIntro: A B Series bolt-action rimfire, and Savage opens its own book by warning that this series is not like its other models. ⛔ THE ACCUTRIGGER IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: the trigger must be pressed squarely over the AccuRelease blade, and a press from the side blocks the sear — you get a click, the rifle does not fire, and the bolt has to be lifted and lowered to recock it. That is designed behaviour, not a fault. ⛔ Cleaning is done with the bolt OUT and from the chamber end, and the bolt assembly itself never comes apart.

steps.title: Safety fully REARWARD to FULL SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger completely away from the trigger and outside the guard, and move the safety fully rearward to FULL SAFE.
steps.prose: On this series FULL SAFE covers the red dot and shows the engraved S. If you can see red, it is not safe — that is the whole indicator.
steps.quote: With the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, your finger completely away from the trigger and out of the trigger guard, move the SAFETY fully rearward to the FULL SAFE position.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — UNLOADING, printed in SECTION 4

steps.title: Magazine out, caught in your hand
steps.action: With one hand ready underneath, pull the latch at the front of the magazine and let the magazine drop into your hand.
steps.prose: Rotary rimfire magazines are moulded and their feed lips are part of the body — drop one on concrete and it is a new magazine, not a repair.
steps.quote: With one hand prepared to catch the detachable magazine, pull the latch at the front of the magazine, ejecting the magazine into your hand (see FIGURE 4).
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — UNLOADING, printed in SECTION 4

steps.title: Bolt lifted and fully back — then look AND feel
steps.action: Hand over the ejection port, finger clear of the trigger, lift the bolt handle slowly and pull it fully rearward to extract whatever is in the chamber. Then look into the chamber and feel it.
steps.prose: Savage prints "LOOK AND FEEL" in capitals for a reason: a .22 case in a dark chamber is genuinely easy to miss by eye alone.
steps.quote: Placing one hand over the ejection port, your finger completely away from the trigger and out of the trigger guard, slowly lift the bolt handle and pull fully rearward to extract the cartridge (if there is one) from the chamber.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — UNLOADING, printed in SECTION 4
steps.warn: LOOK AND FEEL! BE SURE THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE ARE COMPLETELY EMPTY DO NOT ASSUME!

steps.title: Bolt OUT — safety OFF, trigger pulled, bolt withdrawn
steps.action: With the chamber and magazine proven empty and the muzzle safe, move the safety forward to OFF, lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt fully back, then pull the trigger and withdraw the bolt from the rear of the receiver.
steps.prose: ⚠ SAVAGE PRINTS THE INSTALLATION SEQUENCE AND NOT THE REMOVAL ONE — its cleaning instruction is the two words "Remove the bolt." — but Section 3 names the mechanism plainly: the bolt passes the receiver only while the trigger is pulled and the safety is OFF. That is what a bolt which "will not come out" is telling you. Nothing here is invented; the step follows the maker's own installation instruction in reverse and says so.
steps.quote: Firmly pull the trigger (SAFETY must be in the OFF- READY TO FIRE position) while sliding the bolt into the rear of the receiver.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — SECTION 3 – INSTALLING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ FOUR DIGITS ON THE BOLT — check them before it goes back
steps.action: Turn the bolt over. There are four digits engraved on the bottom. They must match the last four digits of the serial number on the receiver. Check that now, while the bolt is out and clean, and check it again before it goes back in.
steps.prose: ⛔ THIS IS THE ONE THING ABOUT A B SERIES THAT AN OWNER MOST NEEDS TO KNOW AND IS MOST LIKELY NOT TO. The bolt is headspaced to ITS OWN rifle, Savage engraves the match on it, and the failure mode of the wrong bolt is not a malfunction — Savage's own words are extensive damage and serious injury. If two of these are ever on the same bench, or a bolt came out of a bag at a range, this check is the whole answer.
steps.quote: BEFORE INSTALLING THE BOLT, VERIFY THAT THE 4 DIGITS ENGRAVED ON THE BOTTOM MATCH THE LAST 4 DIGITS OF THE SERIAL NUMBER ON THE RECEIVER.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — SECTION 3 – INSTALLING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY
steps.warn: BOLT ASSEMBLIES ARE SPECIFICALLY MATCHED TO A FIREARM. USING ANY OTHER BOLT ASSEMBLY MAY CAUSE EXTENSIVE DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM AND/OR SERIOUS INJURY TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDER.

steps.title: Rifle on its side, ejection port DOWN
steps.action: Lay the rifle horizontally with the ejection port facing down, and get a correct-calibre rod, brush, patches, powder solvent and oil together in a ventilated space.
steps.prose: Port down so solvent and loosened fouling fall out of the action instead of down into the trigger group — which on this rifle is the one thing you must not be flushing debris into.
steps.quote: Lay the firearm horizontally with the ejection port facing down.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — CLEANING AND CARE, printed in SECTION 9
steps.warn: NEVER ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE, CLEAN, OR OIL A LOADED FIREARM!

steps.title: ⛔ Bore from the CHAMBER end, out the muzzle
steps.action: A little powder solvent on the brush and push the rod through the barrel several times, entering at the chamber and exiting at the muzzle. Then a patch tip and fresh patches, several times.
steps.prose: ⛔ Every pass in the same direction. With the bolt out you have a clear run at the chamber end, which is exactly why the bolt came out first.
steps.quote: ALWAYS STARTING FROM THE CHAMBER END, PUSH THE CLEANING ROD THROUGH THE BORE AND OUT THE MUZZLE END.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — CLEANING AND CARE, printed in SECTION 9

steps.title: Oiled patch, dry patch, then check the bore is EMPTY
steps.action: Push a patch saturated with gun oil through the bore, then a new dry patch to take the excess out. Then look through the bore and make sure nothing — least of all a piece of patch — has been left in it.
steps.prose: ⛔ Savage names the specific hazard: pieces of cleaning patch. A .22 has a small bore and a torn patch corner wedges in the rifling where it is not obvious.
steps.aside: A VERY THIN FILM OF OIL IS SUFFICIENT PROTECTION – DO NOT OVER OIL!!!
steps.quote: CHECK THE BORE CAREFULLY WHEN DONE TO BE SURE THERE ARE NO OBSTRUCTIONS (I.E. PIECES OF CLEANING PATCH, ETC.).
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — CLEANING AND CARE, printed in SECTION 9

steps.title: Metal surfaces — bolt out, cloth first, then thin oil
steps.action: With the bolt still out so everything is reachable, take mud, twigs and grass off with a soft cloth, then a thin coat of gun oil on all the cleaned metal. Rub where there is any sign of rust. Lightly oil the interior surfaces you can reach.
steps.prose: The bolt raceway and the rear of the barrel are the surfaces that actually rust on a rimfire that lives in a truck, and they are only reachable with the bolt out.
steps.aside: Apply a thin coat of gun oil on all cleaned metal surfaces. Rubbing may be necessary to remove any signs of rust.
steps.quote: In order to be able to reach all surfaces, remove the bolt prior to cleaning and oiling.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — PROTECTING METAL SURFACES, printed in SECTION 9

steps.title: ⛔ Verify the two-position safety, every time
steps.action: When the cleaning is done, put the bolt back and confirm the two-position safety still works in both positions before the rifle goes away.
steps.prose: ⛔ Savage prints this as the closing step of BOTH its cleaning procedures, not as an afterthought. On a rifle whose sear can be blocked by the AccuRelease, confirming the safety is the cheapest check there is.
steps.quote: When done, always verify that the "TWO POSITION SAFETY" is operational as explained in SECTION 2.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — PROTECTING METAL SURFACES, printed in SECTION 9

steps.title: ⛔ Field strip complete — and the bolt stays whole
steps.action: Bolt, magazine, rifle. That is the whole of the routine strip, and the bolt assembly does not come apart.
steps.prose: ⛔ Savage adds the same warning it gives for its autoloaders: bolt assemblies are matched to individual firearms. Strip one rifle at a time so parts cannot be swapped by accident.
steps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — PROTECTING METAL SURFACES, printed in SECTION 9
steps.warn: In depth mechanical issues or questions as well as periodic examinations should be referred to a qualified gunsmith or Savage Arms Service Department.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Bolt open and EMPTY before a screw is touched
deepSteps.action: The deeper job here is taking the stock off, which is what gives access to the AccuTrigger and the underside of the action. Before that: magazine out, bolt lifted and fully rearward, and the chamber checked by eye and by finger.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Savage states the condition explicitly for this procedure, separately from its general safety rules, because what you are about to expose is the trigger mechanism.
deepSteps.quote: BE SURE THE BOLT IS OPEN AND THERE IS NO LIVE AMMUNITION IN EITHER THE CHAMBER OR DETACHABLE MAGAZINE BEFORE REMOVING THE STOCK AND ADJUSTING THE ACCUTRIGGER..
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — SECTION 5 – ACCUTRIGGER ADJUSTMENT

deepSteps.title: Two screws, and they are NOT the same screw
deepSteps.action: Turn the rifle upside down with the muzzle pointing away from you and remove the two stock screws with a 5/32" Allen wrench. ⛔ Note which is which: the REAR action screw has a groove machined in it to tell it from the front one.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The groove is there because the screws are different lengths and putting the wrong one in the wrong hole either bottoms out or leaves the action loose. Savage marks it rather than trusting you to measure.
deepSteps.aside: Using a 5/32" Allen wrench (5/32" for a 'Thumbhole' stock), loosen and remove the two screws securing the stock (see FIGURE 9).
deepSteps.quote: THE REAR ACTION SCREW HAS A GROOVE TO DISTINGUISH IT FROM THE FRONT ACTION SCREW
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — REMOVING THE STOCK, printed in SECTION 5

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Inspect the AccuTrigger for DEBRIS — do not flush it
deepSteps.action: With the stock off, look carefully at the AccuTrigger and its adjustment spring for damage and for foreign debris — twigs, grass, grit. Pick debris out with tweezers or blow it out; do not flood the mechanism with solvent.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This is the reason the stock comes off at all. Debris in the AccuRelease is what makes a rifle click without firing, and Savage names twigs and grass specifically — this is a field rifle and that is what gets in.
deepSteps.quote: With the stock removed, carefully inspect the AccuTrigger and adjustment spring for damage or foreign debris (twigs, grass, etc.).
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — Routine maintenance, printed in SECTION 9

deepSteps.title: While it is apart: bore, barrel, bolt head, stock, rings
deepSteps.action: Look down the bore for obstructions, damage, rust or pitting. Run your fingers down the outside of the barrel feeling for bulges. Inspect the bolt head and extractor. Check the stock and the sling studs. Check the scope rings have not loosened.
deepSteps.prose: Savage's own list, and the barrel-by-feel check is the one worth doing slowly — a bulge you can feel is invisible until you know it is there.
deepSteps.aside: Check the outer surface of the barrel, running your fingers gently down its length, feeling for any bulges or signs of damage.
deepSteps.quote: While the bolt is out, inspect the bolt head, extractor, and all other surfaces for signs for damage or excessive wear.
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — Routine maintenance, printed in SECTION 9
deepSteps.warn: In depth mechanical issues or questions as well as periodic examinations should be referred to a qualified gunsmith or Savage Arms Service Department.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Stock back on — approximately 20 inch-pounds
deepSteps.action: Place the action into the stock, replace both action screws in their own holes, and tighten only enough to secure the stock — approximately 20 inch-pounds.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ A number, and a low one. This is a rimfire in a light stock; over-torquing crushes the bedding and changes where the rifle shoots.
deepSteps.quote: Replace both action screws, tightening only to secure the stock (approximately 20 inch pounds).
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — INSTALLING THE STOCK, printed in SECTION 5

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Then prove the safety before anything is loaded
deepSteps.action: Cycle the bolt several times and confirm it functions properly. Then, with the chamber and magazine empty, the bolt open and the muzzle safe, verify both safety positions. With the safety at FULL SAFE the trigger must have NO movement when pulled.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ "No movement" is the standard, not "does not fire". A trigger that moves at all on FULL SAFE is a rifle that goes to a gunsmith.
deepSteps.aside: WHEN SOMETHING DOES NOT SOUND, FEEL, OR LOOK RIGHT, SEEK THE ADVICE OF A PROFESSIONAL GUNSMITH IMMEDIATELY. NEVER TAKE A CHANCE!
deepSteps.quote: With the SAFETY in the FULL SAFE position, the trigger should have no movement when pulled.
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — B Series Rimfire — Rev 01 09/16 — INSTALLING THE STOCK, printed in SECTION 5

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: ⛔ Bolt OUT, then always from the chamber end
Solvent on the brush, fresh patches after
⛔ Check for patch material before it goes away

cleaning.name: ACTION & BOLT
tasks: Bolt head and extractor wiped and inspected
Bolt raceway and the rear of the barrel
⛔ The bolt assembly does NOT come apart

cleaning.name: METAL SURFACES
tasks: Soft cloth first — mud, twigs, grass
Thin coat of oil, rubbed where rust shows
Lightly oil the reachable interior surfaces

cleaning.name: TRIGGER AREA (stock off)
tasks: ⛔ Inspect the AccuTrigger and its spring for DEBRIS
Pick or blow debris out — do not flood it with solvent
Re-torque both action screws to about 20 inch-pounds

reassembly: ⛔ FIRST: the four digits on the bottom of the bolt must match the last four of the receiver's serial number, and the chamber and magazine must be empty.
Check the bolt handle (the rear portion) is aligned with the front portion of the bolt assembly, and hold the bolt so the FIRING PIN is at top centre.
Line the bolt handle up with the bolt arm slot in the receiver, with the ALIGNMENT NOTCH still centred on the firing pin.
Safety OFF, pull the trigger firmly, and slide the bolt into the rear of the receiver. ⚠ If it will not go, do NOT force it — take it out and recheck the alignment.
Then cycle it several times to be sure it functions.
If the stock came off: action into the stock, both screws in their own holes (the grooved one is the REAR), tightened to approximately 20 inch-pounds.
Verify both positions of the two-position safety with the chamber and magazine empty and the bolt open.
Check the bore is clear of patch material and excess oil before ammunition appears.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber looked at AND felt, muzzle safe. Cycle the bolt several times — it should lift, run and close without grit. With the safety at FULL SAFE the trigger must have NO movement when pulled. Move it forward and dry-fire: press the trigger SQUARELY over the AccuRelease. ⚠ If you get a click and nothing happens, that is the AccuRelease blocking the sear because the press was off to one side — lift and lower the bolt to recock, and try again squarely. Finally, check the bore one more time for patch material.
